issue: On a general remand for resentencing, may the district court consider arguments or evidence that were waived or forfeited at the original sentencing, including a restitution request the government expressly disclaimed?

sides.position: On a general remand, the district court may conduct de novo resentencing and consider any evidence or argument it could have considered originally, including arguments that were waived or forfeited.
cases: United States v. Tat, 97 F.4th 1155 (9th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Moore, 83 F.3d 1231 (10th Cir. 1996)
United States v. Stinson, 97 F.3d 466 (11th Cir. 1996)
United States v. Miclaus, No. 23-3146 (6th Cir. 2026)

quote: Starting with the scope issue, the circuits are split regarding the breadth of a mandate for resentencing on remand.
cite: United States v. Radu Miclaus, No. 23-3146 (6th Cir. 2026)
